L1@P0: NAKAI–MOISHEZON AMPLENESS CRITERION FOR REAL LINE
L2@P0: BUNDLES
L3@P0: OSAMU FUJINO AND KEISUKE MIYAMOTO
L4@P0: Abstract. We show that the Nakai–Moishezon ampleness criterion holds for real line
L5@P0: bundles on complete schemes. As applications, we treat the relative Nakai–Moishezon
L6@P0: ampleness criterion for real line bundles and the Nakai–Moishezon ampleness criterion
L7@P0: for real line bundles on complete algebraic spaces. The main ingredient of this paper is
L8@P0: Birkar’s characterization of augmented base loci of real divisors on projective schemes.

L18@P0: 1. Introduction
L19@P0: Throughout this paper, a scheme means a separated scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed field k of any characteristic. We call such a scheme a variety if it is reduced
L20@P0: and irreducible. Let us start with the definition of R-line bundles.
L21@P0: Definition 1.1 (R-line bundles). Let X be a scheme (or an algebraic space). An R-line
L22@P0: bundle (resp. a Q-line bundle) is an element of Pic(X) ⊗Z R (resp. Pic(X) ⊗Z Q) where
L23@P0: Pic(X) is the Picard group of X.
L24@P0: Similarly, we can define R-Cartier divisors.
L25@P0: Definition 1.2 (R-Cartier divisors). Let X be a scheme. An R-Cartier divisor (resp. a
L26@P0: Q-Cartier divisor) is an element of Div(X)⊗ZR (resp. Div(X)⊗ZQ) where Div(X) denotes
L27@P0: the group of Cartier divisors on X.
L28@P0: We prove the Nakai–Moishezon ampleness criterion for R-line bundles. The following
L29@P0: theorem is the main result of this paper.
L30@P0: Theorem 1.3 (Nakai–Moishezon ampleness criterion for real line bundles on complete
L31@P0: schemes). Let X be a complete scheme over an algebraically closed field and let L be an
L32@P0: R-line bundle on X. Then L is ample if and only if L
L33@P0: dim Z
L34@P0: · Z > 0 for every positivedimensional closed integral subscheme Z ⊂ X.

L37@P0: Key words and phrases. Nakai–Moishezon ampleness criterion, Kleiman’s ampleness criterion, R-line
L38@P0: bundles, R-Cartier divisors, augmented base loci, projectivity, algebraic spaces.

L40@P1: When X is projective, Theorem 1.3 is well known. It was first proved by Campana and
L41@P1: Peternell (see [CP, 1.3. Theorem]). Then a somewhat simpler proof was given by Lazarsfeld
L42@P1: in [La, Theorem 2.3.18]. Unfortunately, their arguments do not work for complete nonprojective schemes because they need an ample line bundle. Moreover, Kleiman’s ampleness
L43@P1: criterion does not always hold for complete nonprojective schemes (see [F1, Section 3] and
L44@P1: [F4, Example 12.1]). Hence we need some new idea to prove Theorem 1.3. By the standard
L45@P1: reduction argument, it is sufficient to treat the case where X is a complete normal variety.
L46@P1: Therefore, all we have to do is to establish the following theorem.
L47@P1: Theorem 1.4 (Nakai–Moishezon ampleness criterion for real Cartier divisors on complete
L48@P1: normal varieties). Let X be a complete normal variety over an algebraically closed field
L49@P1: and let L be an R-Cartier divisor on X. Then L is ample if and only if L
L50@P1: dim Z
L51@P1: · Z > 0 for
L52@P1: every positive-dimensional closed subvariety Z ⊂ X.
L53@P1: For the proof of Theorem 1.4, we use Birkar’s characterization of augmented base loci of
L54@P1: R-divisors on projective schemes (see Theorem 3.4). Hence our approach is different from
L55@P1: those of [CP] and [La]. Although we can not directly apply geometric arguments to R-line
L56@P1: bundles, we can generalize Theorem 1.3 for proper morphisms.
L57@P1: Theorem 1.5 (Relative Nakai–Moishezon ampleness criterion for real line bundles). Let
L58@P1: π : X → S be a proper morphism between schemes and let L be an R-line bundle on X.
L59@P1: Then L is π-ample if and only if L

L62@P1: subscheme Z ⊂ X such that π(Z) is a point.
L63@P1: For the details of the Nakai–Moishezon ampleness criterion and Kleiman’s ampleness
L64@P1: criterion for line bundles, see [Kl]. The reader can find many nontrivial examples of
L65@P1: complete nonprojective varieties in [F1], [F4, Section 12], [FP], and so on. Finally, we prove
L66@P1: the following theorem as an application of Theorem 1.3 by using some basic properties of
L67@P1: algebraic spaces.
L68@P1: Theorem 1.6 (Nakai–Moishezon ampleness criterion for real line bundles on complete
L69@P1: algebraic spaces). Let X be a complete algebraic space over an algebraically closed field
L70@P1: and let L be an R-line bundle on X. Then L is ample if and only if L

L73@P1: every positive-dimensional closed integral subspace Z ⊂ X.
L74@P1: We note that we treat algebraic spaces only in the final section, where we prove Theorem 1.6. We also note that the Nakai–Moishezon ampleness criterion for line bundles on
L75@P1: complete algebraic spaces plays an crucial role in Koll´ar’s projectivity criterion for moduli
L76@P1: spaces (see [Ko] and [F3]).
